messages.author: 4d17bc398c8d91b8
messages.subject: Current state of ODE solvers?
parts:
Hi all,

I know that there's been plenty of talk of adding ODE solving capabilities to stan, and the wiki page sounds promising https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/ODE-Integrator-Support . I did notice that the feature/ode-experimentation has been dormant for a few months. Is there any news on that front?

Alternatively, would it be crazy to code up e.g. Gillespies algorithm and run that each iteration to generate predictions for each new draw of parameter values?

Best regards,
Gustaf

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Current state of ODE solvers?
parts:
The non-stiff ODE solvers should be out in Stan 2.5 (the next
release). You'll find everything, including the relevant doc in
the manual, in feature/issue-771-ode-solver.

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/tree/feature/issue-771-ode-solver

I don't know Gillespies algorithm. We're using a 5th-order Runge-Kutta
solver with interpolation and error control from Boost.

- Bob

messages.author: 22d6bf0e16759db6
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Current state of ODE solvers?
parts:
Hi Gustaf,

If you're talking about Gillespie, that implies you're interested in stochastic simulation, which will be outside the scope of what they're building for Stan.

If I understand it properly, the use case for the Stan ODE solver is a deterministic system with observation error—the underlying dynamics are not stochastic, and there's no process error, so the likelihood comes just from the observation model atop the ODE dynamics. Stan should then let you infer the posterior distribution over parameters governing both the system dynamics as well as the observation model.

If you know you need process noise, you'll have to look elsewhere, e.g., particle filter methods such as the MIF algorithm implemented here:

http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/pomp/index.html

Under MIF, you can generate simulations from stochastic ODEs or Gillespie or anything you like, but the computational cost is very high, because you're effectively integrating over all possible stochastic realizations of the model. (I imagine there are fully Bayesian particle filter-style methods out there as well.)

But you're going to want to start without process noise anyway, and Stan 2.5 should make that easy.

Ed

messages.author: 4d17bc398c8d91b8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Current state of ODE solvers?
parts:
Hi Ed,

Thanks for the comment. I'm currently interested in estimating test kinetics, using Lotka-Volterra ODE's as a simple way to start playing with stuff. I haven't done much in this way before, but came across a reference that suggested Gillespies for LV - it might well be a bad way of going about it. 

I'm going about things in a hierarchical manner atm -it's deterministic with observation error for each person in a population, but each person have their own parameters, drawn from a population-level distribution. It sounds like this would be doable with the Stan ODE solver. I'll be posting the code I'm using now in a separate message, with an explicit solution to a simple ODE -but it's currently running slow as molasses, and I'm hoping there might be something stupid I've done. 

Best,
Gustaf
